Description

ERK1 and ERK2 are switched off by dual-specificity phosphatases that remove both phosphates of the activation loop, and different members of the family do so in different parts of the cell. DUSP6 (MKP-3) is a cytoplasmic phosphatase specific for ERK [1]. Binding ERK through its N-terminal domain switches on its catalytic domain [2]. It removes the phosphotyrosine first, releases ERK phosphorylated on threonine alone, and a second encounter removes the phosphothreonine [3]. DUSP6 shuttles between nucleus and cytoplasm and can hold ERK in the cytoplasm [4]. In the nucleus, DUSP5, whose expression ERK itself induces, dephosphorylates ERK and keeps the inactive kinase there [5, 6]. Binding ERK stabilises DUSP5 [6]. Because ERK held in the nucleus no longer inhibits RAF, DUSP5 paradoxically raises and prolongs ERK activity in the cytoplasm [7]. DUSP3 (VHR) differs from both: it is always present, nuclear and specific for the phosphotyrosine of ERK1 and ERK2, and it inactivates ERK quickly after stimulation and keeps it off in quiescent cells [8]. Cells without DUSP3 overactivate ERK and JNK after serum and arrest in the cell cycle with signs of senescence [9].
